source.title: 22.7 An Inductively-Coupled Wireless Power-Transfer System that is Immune to Distance and Load Variations

trace.notes: Input normalized as a zbMATH resolver URL. Direct zbMATH page reading did not expose a readable record in this environment. Identifier-specific recovery found the same work via DOI 10.1109/ISSCC.2017.7870421, DBLP key conf/isscc/PanARCM17, and NDL/Crossref metadata, then recovered a readable PDF of ISSCC 2017 Session 22 containing the exact title on printed pages 382-383.

Mapped the readable PDF and restricted extraction to section 22.7 on printed pages 382-383. Section structure: title/authors; biomedical-implant motivation and design objective; coupled-resonator analysis; oscillator and automatic-amplitude-control implementation; measured regulation over distance and load; comparison, acknowledgements, references, and figure captions. Notation and terminology identified: k, kC=1/Q2, omega_res, omega_L, omega_H, Q1, Q2, R1, R2, P2, eta, |VS|, |VL|, automatic amplitude control, transmitter, receiver, implant, load, and coil separation. Likely open-problem regions: none.

Scanned the title, body, equations, figure captions, acknowledgements, and references for explicit markers such as Question, Problem, Open, Unknown, Is it true, and Future, and for implicit unresolved research questions. No candidate open or unsolved questions were present. The introductory ideal design objective is immediately followed by the statement that the paper presents an architecture meeting those objectives, so it was not treated as an unresolved problem.
No extracted candidates reached the self-contained rewrite stage.
No candidate clusters were formed because extraction produced no open-question candidates.
